lens: The evidence pool consists entirely of alpha hints on stem cell therapy efficacy across various diseases, but lacks any direct evidence facts on the mechanisms or biomarkers of stem cell exhaustion itself, such as replicative senescence or niche-driven decline. This disconnect prevents the formulation of a publishable thesis on exhaustion, as the available data do not address the core biological processes.
known_to_ignore: Stem cell therapy improves glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) in T1DM patients
Stem cell therapy reduces insulin requirements in T2DM patients
Stem cell therapy enhances progression-free survival in certain hematologic conditions
tensions: Improvements in C-peptide levels post-therapy contrast with no significant change in fasting plasma glucose in diabetes studies
High mortality rates in stem cell transplant-associated acute kidney injury versus generally positive outcomes in other therapeutic contexts
gaps: Direct measurement of stem cell exhaustion markers (e.g., p16INK4a, telomere length) in treated vs. untreated cohorts
Age-stratified analysis of stem cell exhaustion in therapeutic settings
Role of oxidative stress in stem cell exhaustion across different tissue types
reviewer_objections: The thesis lacks primary data linking therapy outcomes to exhaustion mechanisms; it is speculative without cited facts on exhaustion.
Alpha hints are insufficient for evidence-based claims; peer reviewers would demand direct studies on stem cell exhaustion, not just therapy efficacy.
next_extractions: Extract data on stem cell exhaustion biomarkers in age-related disease models from recent publications
Harvest studies comparing stem cell exhaustion rates in different therapeutic dosing regimens
Gather evidence on the impact of oxidative stress on stem cell exhaustion in preclinical diabetes models
